canonical_title: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
description: Interim CEO of Nvidia publicly reaffirmed that the company's open‑source AI strategy remains unchanged following the sudden exit of founder and CEO Jensen Huang. The leadership also reiterated its intention to acquire Hugging Face, despite the leadership transition.

canonical_title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
description: OpenAI announced two new GPT-6.2 variants: Astra, positioned as a frontier model for the hardest projects, and Sol, described as an efficient, versatile model for everyday work. Both are available via the API under the identifiers gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. The models claim better professional outputs, coding assistance, computer‑use capabilities, and higher efficiency at reduced cost. Pricing for Astra is $8 per MTok input and $40 per MTok output, about 80% of the previous GPT‑6 Astra price; Sol is implied to have similar cost reductions.

canonical_title: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents
description: At SC26, NVIDIA’s Ian Buck announced new software for AI agents that can plan experiments, run code and verify results on researchers' own systems, plus the Nemotron for Science processor, the Rubin high‑performance computing GPU, and an expanded Vera CPU platform.

canonical_title: Call-Efficient ICD-10 Code Prediction via Supervised Candidate Generation and Selective LLM Invocation
description: The authors propose a call‑efficient ICD‑10 coding system that first generates candidate codes with a supervised tree‑based model using transformer embeddings, then invokes a large language model only for selected candidates, addressing short noisy diagnosis text, hierarchical label space, and class imbalance.

canonical_title: From Sorry to QED: Refining LLM Math Proofs via Angelic Execution
description: Large language models can now produce Lean proof scripts that capture high‑level mathematical arguments, but the scripts often fail on complex theorems due to missing side conditions or misapplied lemmas. The paper introduces MathEye, a framework that takes these imperfect LLM‑generated scripts and, using angelic execution, automatically fills gaps and corrects errors to produce fully verified Lean proofs.
